solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frenzied attack stopped by bachelor

indicators.note: a thing stopped by something has that something plugged into its middle, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A wild assault is halted by an unmarried man stepping in.
explanation.walkthrough: The raid is split open and the single letter for bachelor is dropped into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid describes someone wildly fanatical or furious, just like a frenzied person out of control.

clue.text: Beside northern river, drinks hot punch

blocks.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, in the north of England

explanation.surface: Someone is sipping a hot punch beside a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot punch' reads as a warm drink, but punch is the definition; the pieces are placed in the order drinks, hot, then the river they sit beside.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundhouse is a wild swinging blow thrown in a boxing or street fight.

clue.text: What are the odds of brash remark showing disdain?

indicators.note: the odds are the odd-numbered positions, so we keep letters one, three and five

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A gambler scoffs at the chances of some cocky remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What are the odds' is a betting phrase, but here it simply asks for the odd letters of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bah is an exclamation used to express contempt or dismissive scorn toward something.

clue.text: Perform work without a couple of learners helping

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these pieces go around another

blocks.note: to do is to perform
op is short for opus, a work
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate; two of them

explanation.surface: Someone does the job with no help from the two trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' seems to be about assistance, but it is a noun: a portion of food. 'Without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of food served onto a plate, a single portion or serving.

clue.text: Flipping gloomy end for Ted and paramour in The Go-Between

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word is read backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: dim means dark or gloomy
the final letter of the name
leman is an archaic word for a lover or paramour

explanation.surface: The Go-Between is L. P. Hartley's novel in which Ted, a farmer, and his lover Marian come to a gloomy end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the novel's plot, and 'Flipping' could be a mild British expletive; in fact the definition is the book's title word.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleman acts as an intermediary between two parties, carrying messages or goods just as a go-between does.

clue.text: Believer has drug overdose first

blocks.note: meth is short for methamphetamine
OD is the standard abbreviation for overdose
1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A person of faith took a drug overdose before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like an ordering instruction, but it is simply 1ST written with I for the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to a Protestant Christian denomination founded by John Wesley, so is one kind of religious believer.

clue.text: Renaissance man rebuffed somewhat more rudely

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of the text is taken
to rebuff is to push back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A cultured gentleman is turned away rather rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters sits across the join of the two final words, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German painter and engraver of the Renaissance era, famous for woodcuts.

clue.text: Funky vibe welcomed by peer’s inamorata?

indicators.note: funky suggests something jazzed up and odd, so the letters are rearranged
to be welcomed by is to be taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman's girlfriend is greeted by a cool atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: The peer's title contains the jumbled atmosphere; the question mark flags that the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovebird is an affectionate term for a lover, so any sweetheart or inamorata can be described that way.

clue.text: Engineering team with precise, great work

indicators.note: engineering means constructing or contriving, so the letters are rebuilt into a new form

blocks.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: An exacting engineering team produces an impressive piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineering' reads as an adjective for the team, but it is the instruction to rework the letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterpiece is an outstanding achievement or the finest creation of an artist or craftsman.

clue.text: I refuse to keep attending western country club

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a flat refusal
at an event is attending it

explanation.surface: Someone declines to stay a member of a club in the west of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' suggests golf, but here it is a club made up of Western countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a military alliance whose members are mostly Western nations.

clue.text: Add padding to covers of Elgar by leading composer

indicators.note: the covers of a book are its outside, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: a team that is up is leading
Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone pads out Elgar's scores with a bit from a greater composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two composers invite a musical reading, but Elgar only donates his outside letters and the composer who leads is Holst.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster furniture is to fit it with stuffing, springs and a fabric covering.

clue.text: Drop in velocity — could that be right?

blocks.note: v is the symbol for velocity in physics formulas
'is it?' asks whether something could be right

explanation.surface: A physicist queries a reading showing a sudden drop in velocity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in velocity' looks like a single physics phrase; the definition is the first two words only.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone is to pay them a casual, informal call at their home.

clue.text: Dirty plate where our food’s served, lacking time?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: a dish is a plate
food is served on our table
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A grimy plate turns up at the family meal table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirty plate' reads as one grubby object, but dirty is the definition and plate starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty in its moral sense means underhand or unscrupulous, lacking honour or integrity.

clue.text: Get angry drunk to recover quickly

blocks.note: to snap is to lose one's temper
out of it is slang for intoxicated

explanation.surface: A drinker gets cross and needs to sober up fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is one sozzled person's evening; the halves are separate slang phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out of a bad mood or daze abruptly is an idiomatic way of saying pull yourself together.

clue.text: Allowed bad similes to be rewritten

indicators.note: rewriting puts material into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fodder

explanation.surface: An editor permits poor comparisons, on condition they are redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' could be the anagram signal, but it is fodder; the instruction is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissible evidence or claims are those permitted or accepted, especially in a court of law.

clue.text: Maybe gents with ball back in sports ground

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the gents is one kind of lav, a toilet
O looks like a ball

explanation.surface: Men return the ball inside the stadium grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' is the British word for a men's toilet, and lav is short for lavatory. The Oval is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in south London is a famous Test cricket venue, and an oval is any elliptical playing field.

clue.text: Suit may be thus taken off, gently going on peg

indicators.note: something going is leaving, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: a pin is a peg
clothes taken off have been stripped
p for piano, the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A suit is removed and hung softly on a peg.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit on a peg sounds like undressing, which is the red herring: the definition describes the suit's pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a pattern of fine vertical lines, typical of formal business suits worn by bankers.

clue.text: Struggle with reversing vehicle? Cars are destroyed here

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word runs right to left

blocks.note: a scrap is a fight or struggle
a dray is a heavy cart

explanation.surface: A driver struggles to back a van, and cars get wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing vehicle' sounds like a clumsy parking attempt; it signals that the cart is written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is a place where old cars are broken up and crushed for metal.

clue.text: Direct channel on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio something is heard, not seen, so we go by sound

blocks.note: a strait is a sea channel

explanation.surface: Tune the radio straight to one station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' seems to mean a radio station, which suits the surface, but here it is a narrow sea passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct and straight both describe a route or manner that goes without deviation or evasion.

clue.text: Tries to ensnare Republican politician in piece of fiction

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a shot is an attempt
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A novelist's plot has attempts to trap a US Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republican letter slips inside the attempts, then the British politician follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A short story is a brief prose narrative, a compact form of fiction.

clue.text: Retailer guided around Italy’s capital

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards
a capital letter heads a word, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: to guide is to lead
the first letter of the country

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper takes a guided tour of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's capital' wants to be Rome; it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared and speciality foods.

clue.text: One making an impression in film dear to the French

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's alien film
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: An actor makes a mark in a film beloved by French audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making an impression' suggests a star wowing an audience; an etcher literally makes impressions from engraved plates.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher cuts designs into metal plates, which are inked to print impressions on paper.

clue.text: Wet weather interrupting sport — test fancy anoraks

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are arranged imaginatively
to interrupt is to break into, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: rain is wet weather
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rain stops play in a cricket Test, and spectators pull on their waterproof jackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anoraks' looks like rain jackets, fitting the weather, but in British slang an anorak is an obsessive hobbyist.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotters, who log locomotive numbers, are the stereotypical British nerds nicknamed after their waterproof coats.

clue.text: Humming Beethoven’s Ninth without certainty

indicators.note: ninth names a position, so only the letter in that place is kept

blocks.note: the ninth letter of the composer's name
iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: Someone hums the Choral Symphony, not quite sure of the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Ninth is his famous symphony, but here it means the ninth letter of his name. Humming is British slang for smelly, and niff is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Niffy and humming are both informal British words for giving off an unpleasant odour, being smelly.

clue.text: West Bank city out of bounds for Spanish runner

indicators.note: the bounds are the edges, and out means removed, so the end letters go

blocks.note: Hebron is a Palestinian city in the West Bank

explanation.surface: A West Bank city is off limits to a Spanish athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: A runner in crosswords is often a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river in northern Spain, flowing to the Mediterranean; rivers run, so a river is a runner.

clue.text: Get misty winter period heading west? Turn the other way

definitions.note: befog means make misty rather than become so

indicators.note: in an across entry, westward is right to left, so the word runs backwards
going the other way means going in reverse, so this word is read backwards too

blocks.note: Feb is short for February, a winter month
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Mist descends in a cold spell out west, so turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a verb telling you what to do; it is a noun, a go.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to envelop in fog or obscure, making something misty or unclear.

clue.text: Full B&B has to change light source

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fodder
fodder, the two letters without the ampersand
fodder

explanation.surface: A fully booked guesthouse has to replace a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' does double duty in the surface but its letters join the mix; B&B is bed and breakfast, a small guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashbulb gives a brief intense burst of light for photography, so it is a source of illumination.

clue.text: Where one might study e.g. Watt or Kelvin briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the watt and the kelvin are units of measurement

explanation.surface: A student might study the physicists Watt or Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: The two famous Scottish scientists are named here for units named after them, not for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is informal British shorthand for university, the place where students go to study for degrees.

clue.text: What overzealous Remainer did is exposed, gathering support

indicators.note: to gather is to take in, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: to be outed is to be exposed
a stay is a supporting prop

explanation.surface: A keen Remain campaigner is exposed while rounding up backers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remainer suggests Brexit, when Remainers wanted Britain to stay in the EU; read literally, a remainer is someone who stays, and an overzealous one stays too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay a welcome is to remain longer than wanted, exactly what an overeager stayer would do.

clue.text: Sunshine, we hear, giving boost

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: rays of sunshine

explanation.surface: Sunshine is said to lift one's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunshine arrives as beams of light, which sound identical to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to lift or increase it, the same sense as to raise.
